sam_jordan: heads-up — customer (private/vpc) seeing steady 200-400ms extra tail latency and a bunch of requests routed to ap-southeast-1 IPs even though their deployment is pinned to us-east-1. They reported this started after a partner network change.

maria_ops: can you paste a sample traceroute / dig from their pod?

sam_jordan: sure — grabbed from their debug pod, anonymized: 
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.private
52.62.11.44
$ curl -sv --resolve api.redwood.private:443:52.62.11.44 https://api.redwood.private/health
*   Trying 52.62.11.44:443... connected.
* TLS 1.2 connection using ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.private
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
traceroute to 52.62.11.44 (AS 1337) shows hops through our partner transit -> peers in SIN.
```
traceroute output (snip):
 8  tg-peer.example.net (10.100.8.1)  18.2 ms  18.0 ms  17.9 ms
 9  203.64.12.5 (203.64.12.5)  44.6 ms  45.1 ms  46.2 ms
 10  52.62.11.44 (52.62.11.44)  47.0 ms  46.8 ms  47.2 ms
```

They resolve api.redwood.private to a public IP that geolocates to SIN (52.62.x.x).

taylor_support: thanks — do they use internal DNS forwarding (VPC+onprem resolver) or split-horizon?

sam_jordan: internal resolver is onprem -> VPC resolver (172.16.2.10). It looks like their DNS frwd is returning our edge anycast IP that currently has an active BGP path to SIN from the partner.

kiran_infra: oh, we hit this before — partner advertised a more specific route to our edge anycast from SIN region so traffic gets hairpinned. Two quick checks: 1) which EIP is returned and its geolocation, 2) VPC route tables and TGW attachments preference.

maria_ops: i dug into their VPC RTs — private subnet -> TGW attachment to partner (higher priority) vs NAT gateway in same AZ (lower priority). So route selects partner path. That matches traceroute.

sam_jordan: ok that explains wrong-region selection. Customer expects egress to use local NAT in us-east. What about why DNS pointed at that specific EIP?

kiran_infra: our edge uses anycast; the partner's BGP announcement made SIN the best path for that anycast IP from their colo. Their resolver forwarded the anycast IP as-is. So twofold: DNS returned anycast EIP; routing chooses TGW->partner which sends to SIN.

taylor_support: proposed mitigation steps? customer needs low latency now.

kiran_infra: immediate: update their subnet route table to prefer local NAT (replace TGW target with nat-gw-id) for the affected prefixes (or add more specific route to 52.62.0.0/16 -> nat-gw). Medium-term: ask partner to withdraw the more-specific BGP announcement for our edge anycast or tag their peer session to prefer us-east.

maria_ops: we also suggested they tweak their internal resolver to rewrite API names to the private VPC endpoint (split-horizon), or mask with internal ALB private IP so DNS doesn't leak anycast EIP.

sam_jordan: i pushed those steps to the customer: 1) change route table for service subnets to use nat-0abc.. (we walked them through Console CLI) 2) change DNS forwarder to prefer VPC resolver for redwood hostnames 3) open ticket with partner to remove specific BGP ad.

devops-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-2345 — "Private VPC egress routing -> partner BGP causing wrong-region egress" assigned to kiran_infra.

taylor_support: customer applied route change and reports tail latency dropped to +20ms (was +200ms). They still see occasional hits to SIN during failover windows. we recommended adding an explicit egress policy in their redwood-private config: "preferred_region: us-east-1" so our runtime will prefer local variants when available.

kiran_infra: follow-ups: 1) I'll coordinate with partner to remove the specific announcement. 2) infra will add a diagnostic alert when traceroutes to anycast EIP deviate geo (TGW path change). 3) doc: add troubleshooting checklist for "private egress -> wrong region".

sam_jordan: thanks — I'll mark this thread as resolved for the customer and paste remediation steps into the support ticket. cc @maria_ops @kiran_infra : can one of you open the internal runbook PR with the checklist? 

maria_ops: will do, PR incoming. :white_check_mark:
